problems.why: 受 opens this word, so it cannot use the -う.け slot: the leading hyphen marks うけ as it appears when 受 is NOT word-initial (引き受け, 待ち受け, 荷受け). The span うけ and the sound are right, but the slot's defining property is contradicted by every word filed in it. The け-only okurigana is the ren'youkei stem of 受ける used as the first half of a compound verb, so the lemma slot is う.ける — which is where the pre-alignment grouping had all five, and where the aligner still puts 引き受ける (受 genuinely non-initial) and 受付. The exact-okurigana-match preference picked け over ける and overrode the hyphen.

Phonetic ateji for 'Africa'. 加=カ is technically its real on-reading, so the alignment is not a sound error, but the word is an obsolete 音訳 spelling, not an example of the カ reading in use. The same entry already files its sibling 亜米利加/アメリカ under irregular (only because 米 has no メ reading, not on principle), so the two country-name ateji are treated inconsistently inside one kanji page. Reported as a consistency/pedagogy call, not a mis-read: showing アフリカ as an example word for カ next to 参加/増加/追加 is misleading.
